wps.title: the BlockOnPossibleDataLoss reader: every check DacFx writes, read from its own script and run read-only
wps.brief: Build WP 2.2 of V3_MILESTONES.md (§8; read its row in full, §1 fact 3, §4 rows 17 and 20, WP 1.4 and WP 1.5). Spike S2 is on the base and is this work package's specification: read its receipts (tests/Golden/data-loss-checks/, tests/Io.Tests/BlockOnPossibleDataLossCheckTests.cs and BlockOnPossibleDataLossChecks.cs, DECISIONS.md's S2 lines) and S2's notes on what WP 2.2 should read, at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/specs/s2-notes.txt. In io (named for the concept, beside io/SqlServer's plan): drop SQLCMD directive lines; substitute $(var) in memory from the environment's SQLCMD values, the substituted text never written or printed (WP 1.5); parse with TSql160Parser; collect each IF EXISTS (...) RAISERROR at state 127 (§1 fact 3) with its table and the statements it protects, telling it apart from the constraint-verification RAISERROR that also uses state 127 and from a table rebuild's copy step that reuses the IF EXISTS predicate with a BEGIN ... INSERT ... END body, as S2 measured; regenerate the predicate with io's Sql160ScriptGenerator and run it as SELECT CASE WHEN EXISTS (<predicate>) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END through SqlServer.Measure, so it passes AggregateQuery.Of's allowlist; fill the kernel's site record that WP 2.1a defined (kernel/Preconditions.cs) so Preconditions.Of reads TableEmpty from it. Done when: the reader finds exactly the checks S2 extracted, from both DacFx releases (run the 162.5.57 half through tests/DacFx162/), and each predicate, run on a copy, answers 1 on a populated table and 0 on an empty one. Safety, word for word to WP 1.4 and WP 1.5: the predicate passes the allowlist or the site refuses; a SQLCMD value marked sensitive never appears in any output, log or error; against an environment classified real a failed query reports its error number and site only. Update V3_PARITY.md's rows the reader now holds (PAR-020 and PAR-201 read the check from DacFx's own script; PAR-222), keeping clauses that wait on WP 2.5 or WP 4.5 in the grammar ParityResolves accepts. Per-file budget: 500 lines a code file, 140 characters a line.

wps.title: kernel Witness: the existing-data tier's plan, ported test-first from the Facsimile's planter cases
wps.brief: Build WP 3.8 of V3_MILESTONES.md (§9; the operator confirmed the re-cut on 2026-10-19). The operator asked that the recent write-up on the Twin and its proposed MCP inform this work: read archive/v2/TWIN_SUCCESSION.md and the Facsimile's TARGET.md (its MCP surface), HANDOFF.md, README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md (its §5 copy build and the planter) and INVARIANTS.md under archive/v2/ssdt-agent/facsimile/, then its cases/20-planter.md, which this work package ports test-first. Kernel only: kernel Witness, the rows to plant table by table, from the copy's Schema (kernel/Schema*.cs, WP 3.1, on the base), Order (kernel/Order.cs), the preconditions and an ExistingData (kernel/Preconditions.cs): one valid row where the environment has rows, with its NOT NULL foreign-key ancestors (an ancestor reuses a seeded row before a new one is planted); one violating row for each precondition answered violating, per value or collation class (WP 2.3 counts the classes in io/AggregateQueries*.cs; the kernel names them as data, never by calling io); per table the largest of its needs, not their sum; a child linked to a planted or seeded parent wherever the change validates a foreign key, so the copy holds no orphan the environment lacks; values in nullable columns, so a populated but clean table stays clean. Literals are ordinal and fitted to each column's width (kernel/ColumnType.cs's facets), with no Random, no clock and no seed, and none comes from an environment. Without an ExistingData, a few presence rows per table. This work package is the plan only, typed values per column in Order's order; WP 3.5 plants them as ScriptDom INSERTs. Where ordinal literals cannot satisfy a check constraint, the plan names the table and the check as planter-needs-row (§9 'Watch for'), a refusal the agent answers by writing one valid row; its exit (8 needs-input, by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-19) joins cli/exits.frozen with the verb that first surfaces it, not here. The kinds are the six WP 2.1a holds; WP 2.1's second slice adds the statement-shown kinds next wave and extends the planter, so make a new kind one case. Done when: every pure case of cases/20-planter.md for these kinds passes, its case identifier in the test name or InlineData; two plans from the same inputs are identical (D1); a schema edit changes only the touched tables' rows (D3); CsCheck properties for both. Name these tests where VALUES.md's planted forms of D6, P1, P2 and P3 still say pending, and in V3_PARITY.md PAR-032 ('the planter's plan — not held yet: WP 3.8'), keeping PAR-030 and PAR-031's clauses that wait on WP 3.6. Per-file budget: Appendix F plans Witness.cs at 500, so split it by concept to stay within 500 lines a file and 140 characters a line.

wps.brief: Spikes S9, S10 and S11 of V3_MILESTONES.md (§6, the spikes table; the Facsimile's §11 questions 1, 9 and 10 in archive/v2/ssdt-agent/facsimile/ARCHITECTURE.md, its F5 and F9; archive/v2/TWIN_SUCCESSION.md §2 and §6b). A scout ran all three in scratch on both releases and specified the receipts: read /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-outsystems-ddl-exporter/17755096-5809-5c10-a22d-d46e8371455a/scratchpad/specs/2-spikes-s9-s10-and-s11-trust-state-th.json end to end. Its measurements: S9, Extract and LoadFromDatabase keep a disabled check and foreign key (CheckConstraint.Disabled, ForeignKeyConstraint.Disabled) and keep untrusted only as the internal annotation IsNotTrustedPropertyAnnotation, with no public property, and a publish of the extracted package reproduces both, but v3 builds its base from the repository, so the trust step must read trust from the catalog (sys.foreign_keys and sys.check_constraints is_not_trusted and is_disabled, through SqlServer.Measure); S10, on both releases validation runs after the post-deploy script; S11, system-named constraints keep their names only if the environment's database has history, so the test must give it history (objects created and dropped) before its publish.
